extracted.intended_audience: public water system operators, State drinking water regulators, and compliance officers responsible for implementing and enforcing 40 CFR part 141
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and performance/monitoring criteria for disinfection and filtration of public drinking water systems (turbidity limits, CT inactivation requirements, residual disinfectant monitoring, analytical methods, sampling frequencies, reporting). Applicable to systems using surface water or groundwater under the direct influence of surface water.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residual disinfectant detectability limit (non-filtration systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: The residual disinfectant concentration in the distribution system, measured as total chlorine, combined chlorine, or chlorine dioxide, cannot be undetectable in more than 5 percent of the samples each month, for any two consecutive months that the system serves water to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Water in the distribution system with a heterotrophic bacteria concentration less than or equal to 500/ml (HPC) is deemed to have a detectable disinfectant residual for this requirement. The value 'V' in the formula (definitions of a, b, c, d, e provided) cannot exceed 5 percent in one month, for any two consecutive months. Definitions: a = instances where residual is measured; b = instances where residual not measured but HPC measured; c = residual measured but not detected and no HPC measured; d = residual measured but not detected and HPC >500/ml; e = residual not measured and HPC >500/ml.

rubrics_metrics.name: State exemption for HPC analysis lack (non-filtration systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the State determines, based on site-specific considerations, that a system has no means for having a sample transported and analyzed for HPC by a certified laboratory under the requisite time and temperature conditions and that the system is providing adequate disinfection in the distribution system, the 5% undetectable residual requirement does not apply to that system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemption is conditional on State determination of both lack of means to transport/analyze HPC under §141.74(a)(1) conditions and adequate disinfection in the distribution system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinfection requirements for systems providing filtration
rubrics_metrics.description: Each public water system that provides filtration treatment must provide disinfection treatment such that the total treatment processes of that system achieve at least 99.9 percent (3-log) inactivation and/or removal of Giardia lamblia cysts and at least 99.99 percent (4-log) inactivation and/or removal of viruses, as determined by the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residual disinfectant concentration in water entering the distribution system cannot be less than 0.2 mg/l for more than 4 hours. Distribution residual detectability rule (undetectable ≤5% monthly for two consecutive months) applies (see separate entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: State exemption for HPC analysis lack (filtered systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the State determines, based on site-specific considerations, that a system has no means for having a sample transported and analyzed for HPC by a certified laboratory under the requisite time and temperature conditions and that the system is providing adequate disinfection in the distribution system, the 5% undetectable residual requirement in paragraph (b)(3)(i) does not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same conditional exemption rules as for non-filtered systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtration requirement and compliance deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: A public water system that uses a surface water source or a ground water source under the direct influence of surface water, and does not meet all criteria in §141.71(a) and (b) for avoiding filtration, must provide both disinfection (§141.72(b)) and filtration treatment complying with §141.73 by June 29, 1993, or within 18 months of failure to meet any criterion for avoiding filtration, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to meet any requirement of §141.73 after the specified date is a treatment technique violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turbidity limit for conventional or direct filtration
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems using conventional filtration or direct filtration, the turbidity level of representative samples of a system's filtered water must be ≤ 0.5 NTU in at least 95 percent of the measurements taken each month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured as specified in §141.74(a)(1) and (c)(1). The State may substitute a higher turbidity limit if it determines the system can still achieve at least 99.9% Giardia removal at that higher turbidity, but in no case may the State approve a turbidity limit that allows more than 1 NTU in more than 5 percent of the samples taken each month. Also turbidity must at no time exceed 5 NTU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute turbidity maximum (all filtration types)
rubrics_metrics.description: The turbidity level of representative samples of a system's filtered water must at no time exceed 5 NTU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to conventional, direct, slow sand, diatomaceous earth, and other filtration technologies; measured per §141.74(a)(1) and (c)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Turbidity limits for slow sand filtration
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems using slow sand filtration, the turbidity level of representative samples of filtered water must be ≤ 1 NTU in at least 95 percent of the measurements taken each month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured as specified in §141.74(a)(1) and (c)(1). The State may substitute a higher turbidity limit if it determines there is no significant interference with disinfection at that higher level. The turbidity must at no time exceed 5 NTU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turbidity limits for diatomaceous earth filtration
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems using diatomaceous earth filtration, the turbidity level of representative samples of filtered water must be ≤ 1 NTU in at least 95 percent of the measurements taken each month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured as specified in §141.74(a)(1) and (c)(1). The turbidity must at no time exceed 5 NTU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of other filtration technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: A public water system may use a filtration technology not listed in paragraphs (a)–(c) if it demonstrates to the State, using pilot plant studies or other means, that the alternative filtration technology, in combination with disinfection treatment meeting §141.72(b), consistently achieves 99.9% removal/inactivation of Giardia lamblia and 99.99% removal/inactivation of viruses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a system that makes this demonstration, the requirements of paragraph (b) apply. Deadlines for different population sizes are specified (§141.173 and §§141.550–141.553).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use only specified or EPA-approved analytical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the analytical method(s) specified in §141.74(a) or otherwise approved by EPA may be used to demonstrate compliance with §§141.71, 141.72 and 141.73.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurements for pH, turbidity, temperature and residual disinfectant concentrations must be conducted by a person approved by the State. Total coliforms, fecal coliforms and HPC must be conducted by a laboratory certified by the State or EPA to do such analysis. Incorporation by reference of Standard Methods and other cited methods is specified; copies and inspections locations described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample holding time and temperature for fecal/HPC analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The time from sample collection to initiation of analysis for fecal coliforms and HPC may not exceed 8 hours, and systems must hold samples below 10 °C during transit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is specified in the footnotes to the analytical methods section and is a condition for using HPC as a surrogate for residual detectability determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved analytical methods for organisms and turbidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Public water systems must conduct analysis of pH, temperature, total coliforms, fecal coliforms, heterotrophic bacteria, and turbidity in accordance with methods listed at §141.23(k)(1) or one of the analytical methods listed (Standard Methods codes, SimPlate, Hach FilterTrak, etc.), alternative methods listed in appendix A to subpart C, and Technical Notes on Drinking Water Methods (EPA-600/R-94-173).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation includes detailed method citations (e.g., Standard Methods 9221, 9222, 9215, 2130B, etc.) and references for obtaining method documents and online versions. Certain method substitutions (e.g., lactose broth for lauryl tryptose broth) are permitted under specified validation conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed methods and continuous monitoring for residual disinfectant
rubrics_metrics.description: Public water systems must measure residual disinfectant concentrations with one of the analytical methods listed or alternative methods approved. If approved by the State, DPD colorimetric test kits or ITS free chlorine test strips may be used. Free and total chlorine residuals may be measured continuously if adapted with equivalent chemistry, accuracy, and precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruments used for continuous monitoring must be calibrated with a grab sample measurement at least every five days, or with a State-approved protocol for calibration. Test strip and method document sources are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source water coliform sampling frequency (non-filtering systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fecal coliform or total coliform density measurements must be performed on representative source water samples immediately prior to the first or only point of disinfectant application at the following minimum weekly frequency: ≤500 persons: 1 sample/week; 501–3,300: 2/week; 3,301–10,000: 3/week; 10,001–25,000: 4/week; >25,000: 5/week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Samples must be taken on separate days. Additionally, one fecal or total coliform density measurement must be made every day the system serves water to the public and source turbidity exceeds 1 NTU (these count toward weekly requirement), unless the State determines the system cannot have the sample analyzed within 30 hours for logistical reasons outside system control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source water turbidity monitoring frequency (non-filtering systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Turbidity measurements required by §141.71(a)(2) must be performed on representative grab samples of source water immediately prior to the first or only point of disinfectant application every four hours (or more frequently) that the system serves water to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A system may substitute continuous turbidity monitoring for grab sampling if it validates continuous measurement accuracy on a regular basis using a State-approved protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily CT-based total inactivation ratio determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The total inactivation ratio for each day the system is in operation must be determined based on the CT99.9 values in tables 1.1–1.6, 2.1, and 3.1, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameters necessary to determine the total inactivation ratio must be monitored as follows: temperature measured at least once per day at each residual sampling point; if chlorine is used, pH measured at least once per day at each chlorine residual sampling point; disinfectant contact time(s) 'T' determined each day during peak hourly flow; residual disinfectant concentration(s) 'C' before or at the first customer measured each day during peak hourly flow. Systems using disinfectants other than chlorine may demonstrate alternate CT99.9 values to the State via a State-approved protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: CT99.9 tables and interpolation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: CT values (CT99.9) for 99.9 percent inactivation of Giardia lamblia cysts are provided for free chlorine at multiple temperatures and pH values (tables 1.1–1.6), and for chlorine dioxide, ozone (table 2.1), and chloramines (table 3.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CT values between indicated pH values may be determined by linear interpolation. CT values between indicated temperatures of different tables may be determined by linear interpolation; if no interpolation is used, use the CT99.9 value at the lower temperature and at the higher pH (guidance varies slightly by table). Some CT tables note these values achieve greater than 99.99% inactivation of viruses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation methods for total inactivation ratio (one or multiple disinfectant points)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the system uses only one point of disinfectant application, compliance may be shown either by a single inactivation ratio CTcalc/CT99.9 ≥ 1.0 determined before or at the first customer during peak hourly flow, or by successive CTcalc/CT99.9 values representing sequential inactivation ratios between the point of disinfectant application and a point before or at the first customer (method in paragraph (b)(4)(i)(B)). If the system uses more than one point of disinfectant application, the CT of each disinfection sequence must be determined immediately prior to the next point and CTcalc/CT99.9 of each sequence must be calculated to determine compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation provides an explicit method for combining successive CT sequences to obtain a total inactivation ratio; total percent inactivation calculation is allowed though not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring residual disinfectant entering distribution (continuous monitoring requirement and grab-sampling alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: The residual disinfectant concentration of the water entering the distribution system must be monitored continuously, and the lowest value must be recorded each day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If continuous monitoring equipment fails, grab sampling every 4 hours may be conducted in lieu of continuous monitoring for no more than 5 working days following equipment failure. Systems serving 3,300 or fewer persons may take grab samples in lieu of providing continuous monitoring on an ongoing basis at specified daily frequencies (table provided: <500:1 sample/day; 501–1,000:2/day; 1,001–2,500:3/day; 2,501–3,300:4/day). If residual falls below 0.2 mg/l in a grab-sampling system, take grab samples every 4 hours until ≥0.2 mg/l.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of residual disinfectant sampling with total coliform sampling points and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Until March 31, 2016, residual disinfectant concentration must be measured at least at the same points in the distribution system and at the same time as total coliforms are sampled as specified in §141.21. Beginning April 1, 2016, the requirement references §§141.854–141.858.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State may allow a system that uses both surface water and groundwater under direct influence to take disinfectant residual samples at other points if more representative of treated water quality within the distribution system. Heterotrophic bacteria (HPC) may be measured in lieu of residual disinfectant concentration. The State may exempt systems that cannot transport/analyze HPC under requisite conditions if adequate disinfection is demonstrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring requirements for systems using filtration treatment (turbidity & residual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems that provide filtration must monitor according to §141.73 beginning June 29, 1993 or when filtration is installed. Turbidity measurements of filtered water must be performed every four hours (or more frequently) that the system serves water to the public; continuous monitoring may substitute if validated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For systems using slow sand filtration or filtration treatment other than conventional/direct/diatomaceous earth, the State may reduce sampling frequency to once per day if it determines less frequent monitoring is sufficient. For systems serving ≤500 persons, the State may reduce turbidity sampling to once per day regardless of filtration type if sufficient. Residual disinfectant entering distribution must be monitored continuously with grab-sampling exceptions and sample-frequency table for small systems (see separate entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirement for source water quality (non-filtering systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: A public water system that uses a surface water source and does not provide filtration treatment must report monthly to the State specified information; source water quality information must be reported to the State within 10 days after the end of each month the system serves water to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies beginning December 31, 1990 (with timelines for groundwater under direct influence and State-specified alternative reporting if State has already determined filtration is required).
